key_insight: A world model can learn what stays the same while missing the changes needed to control an environment. The paper identifies this failure as “static collapse”: representations retain episode-specific static content but suppress manipulation-relevant changes.
problem_solved: Distributional regularization alone does not guarantee control-relevant representations in JEPA-style world models. Static features can remain diverse across episodes and predictable over time, allowing important state changes to be overlooked.
method: Study JEPA-style models that predict action-conditioned latent dynamics without reconstructing observations.
Identify static collapse by distinguishing preserved static content from suppressed manipulation-relevant changes.
The title proposes motion-guided contrastive regularization; the supplied abstract is truncated and does not specify its implementation or results.
impact: For practitioners, predictable and diverse latent features are not necessarily useful for control. Evaluating whether representations capture action-relevant changes is important when developing world models.

paper_title: Motion-guided Contrastive Regularization For Latent World Models
